name: I–V–vi–iii–IV
note: Bass falls a fourth, rises a step, then cadences.

name: Circle progression
note: Roots fall in fifths through all seven degrees.

name: Three-chord trick
note: The key's three major chords; V pulls home.

name: I–IV–I–V
note: Home, away, home again, then V turns it.

name: IV–V–I
note: Predominant, dominant, tonic: the full cadence.

name: ii–V–I
note: Predominant ii, dominant V, home.

name: Authentic cadence
note: V7 resolves to I; the strongest close.

name: Plagal cadence
note: IV to I; the soft amen close.

name: Minor plagal
note: IV's third slips down a half step, then home.

name: Double plagal
note: Two falling fourths: bVII to IV to I.

name: Deceptive cadence
note: V promises home, then lands on vi.

name: Deceptive to bVI
note: V7 swerves to borrowed bVI instead of home.

name: Half cadence
note: Phrase pauses on V, asking for more.

name: 50s progression
note: Tonic, relative minor, then IV and V lift home.

name: I–vi–ii–V
note: ii replaces IV; roots then fall in fifths to V.

name: I–V–vi–IV
note: Four chords cycling; ending on IV keeps it open.

name: Royal road
note: IV and V lift, then iii slips into vi.

name: I–IV–V–IV
note: V falls back to IV before home; garage staple.

name: I–bVII–IV
note: bVII falls to IV, then home; no V needed.

name: Mixolydian vamp
note: Two major chords a whole step apart.

name: bVI–bVII–I
note: Borrowed bVI and bVII climb by steps to I.

name: I–bIII–IV
note: Borrowed bIII gives the blues-rock riff its bite.

name: 12-bar blues
note: I, IV and V as dominant sevenths over twelve bars.

name: Quick-change blues
note: The 12-bar with IV in bar 2.

name: 8-bar blues
note: I, V, two bars of IV, then I–V twice.

name: V–IV–I–V
note: Last four bars of the 12-bar, turning back.

name: I7–IV7 vamp
note: Two dominant sevenths trading; no need to resolve.

name: ii–V–I
note: Each seventh falls a half step to the next third.

name: Backdoor ii–V
note: Borrowed iv7 and bVII7 reach I from below.

name: Tritone sub ii–V–I
note: bII7 replaces V7; the bass slides down by half steps.

name: Jazz turnaround
note: vi, ii and V fall in fifths back to I.

name: I–VI7–ii–V
note: Major VI7 points hard at ii.

name: I–#i°7–ii–V
note: A passing diminished seventh climbs from I to ii.

name: Ragtime progression
note: Dominant sevenths chain down in fifths to I.

name: Double dominant
note: II7 is V of V; it pushes into V7.

name: I–II7–ii–V
note: II7 softens to ii7 before V7.

name: I–IV vamp
note: Major sevenths drifting between I and IV.

name: I–I7–IV–iv
note: I7 leans into IV; iv darkens the return.

name: IV–#iv°7–I
note: Bass climbs a half step; I often over its fifth.

name: V–#v°7–vi
note: A passing diminished seventh lifts V into vi.

name: I–III–IV–iv
note: Major III lifts, then iv turns it bittersweet.

name: Lydian vamp
note: Major II raises the fourth; floating, unresolved.

name: Chromatic mediant
note: Roots a major third apart, sharing one note.

name: Monte
note: Rises: V7/IV–IV, V7/V–V; classically I6/5 and II6/5.

name: Fonte
note: Falls: V7/ii–ii, V7–I; classically in inversion.

name: Andalusian cadence
note: Bass walks down the scale to a major V.

name: Aeolian vamp
note: VI and VII rock back and forth below i.

name: i–VI–VII
note: VI and VII climb back to i.

name: Aeolian cadence
note: VI and VII climb by steps to i.

name: i–VI–III–VII
note: Natural minor loop; III and VII add light.

name: i–III–VII–IV
note: Dorian major IV turns the loop back to i.

name: i–III–IV
note: Dorian major IV after III; a rising rock loop.

name: i–iv–V
note: Harmonic-minor V gives the loop its leading tone.

name: i–iv–v
note: Natural minor triads; no leading tone.

name: i–I7–iv
note: Major I7 turns i into the dominant of iv.

name: Dorian vamp
note: Major IV adds Dorian's raised sixth.

name: Double tonic
note: i and VII alternate; no V needed.

name: Minor blues
note: Minor i and iv; VI7 slides into V7.

name: Minor ii–V–i
note: Half-diminished ii and V7 pull into minor i.

name: Circle progression
note: Roots fall in fifths through every scale degree.

name: La Folia
note: Baroque ground; first half ends on V, second on i.

name: Neapolitan cadence
note: Usually bII6, bass on 4; half step above i.

name: Half cadence
note: iv to major V; the phrase pauses.

name: iv–vii°7–i
note: Leading-tone seventh chord resolves to i.

name: Picardy third
note: Minor phrase ends on a major I.

name: iv–V–i
note: Minor iv, major V, home: the full minor cadence.

name: Authentic cadence
note: Raised leading tone in V7 resolves to i.

name: Plagal cadence
note: iv to i; a dark amen.

name: Phrygian vamp
note: bII sits a half step above i.

name: i–iv vamp
note: Two minor sevenths a fourth apart.

name: Minor turnaround
note: VI, ii and V lead back to minor i.
